## Synthesis: final code-review report

5 findings survived independent verification (high-effort review). They are numbered [0]-[4] below.

### [0] all_hanta.py:3290 (CONFIRMED)
The opt-in --phylogenetics block was inserted before the 'Writing outputs' section instead of after it, so any exception/SystemExit raised while running the phylogenetics stage (missing mafft/iqtree binaries, missing biopython/dendropy, or any bug in parse_cds_fasta/collect_phylo_candidates/run_phylogenetics_stage) aborts run_pipeline before a single one of the standard parquet/json outputs (ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, ortho_ml_*, ortho_qc_report, ortho_summary.json, etc.) is written.
Failure scenario: A user runs `python all_hanta.py --phylogenetics` in an environment where mafft/iqtree aren't on PATH (or biopython/dendropy aren't installed) -- exactly the setup mistake the README explicitly warns about ('don't just prepend that env's bin/ to PATH'). resolve_binary()/the ImportError check in run_phylogenetics_stage raises SystemExit, which propagates uncaught out of run_pipeline and main(). Because 'logging.info("Writing outputs")' and every safe_write_parquet/safe_write_json call for the core (non-phylogenetics) tables now sit textually after the `if args.phylogenetics:` block, none of them execute: the entire run produces zero output tables (not even ortho_summary.json), even though this feature is documented and designed to be strictly additive/opt-in and the core pipeline is supposed to be unaffected by it. The user loses the whole run over an unrelated, easily-fixed environment issue instead of just missing ortho_reassortment_table.parquet.
Verifier evidence: all_hanta.py lines 3290-3301: the `if args.phylogenetics:` block (which calls `run_phylogenetics_stage(...)` at line 3294) sits textually before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` at line 3301 and all the `safe_write_parquet`/`safe_write_json` calls for the core tables (lines 3302-3317, including `ortho_summary.json`). There is no try/except around this block in run_pipeline. Inside run_phylogenetics_stage (line 2555), missing biopython/dendropy triggers `raise SystemExit(...)` at line 2568, and missing mafft/iqtree triggers `resolve_binary()` (line 2305) to `raise SystemExit(...)` at line 2310 -- both uncaught, both reachable before any core output table is written. So `python all_hanta.py --phylogenetics` in an environment lacking mafft/iqtree/biopython/dendropy on PATH aborts the whole pipeline with zero output tables written, not just a missing reassortment table.

### [1] all_hanta.py:2496 (CONFIRMED)
The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not Phylo.read, the patristic-distance/RF computation, or bootstrap-support lookup, so it only partially re-establishes the 'never aborts the run' invariant it claims (and that transform_one_record's whole-body try/except actually delivers) for a phylogenetics-stage isolate.
Failure scenario: For a species whose IQ-TREE tree is missing a tip that write_segment_fasta wrote (e.g. IQ-TREE silently dropped a duplicate/near-identical sequence during ModelFinder, a known IQ-TREE behavior with `--seqtype DNA` on near-identical CDS), _patristic_distance_matrix's `clades[labels[i]]` lookup (line ~2364, called via tree_divergence_for_species at line 2507) raises KeyError outside the try/except. Because run_phylogenetics_stage (line 2555) and its caller in run_pipeline (line 3294) have no surrounding try/except either, the KeyError propagates uncaught and crashes the whole pipeline run -- not just marking that species 'failed' as documented in the docstring/README, but losing the run entirely, including the ortho_accession_table/species/isolate/ML parquet writes that come after this block (lines 3301+).
Verifier evidence: The try/except at all_hanta.py:2496-2503 wraps only run_mafft/run_iqtree; `trees[segment] = Phylo.read(...)` (line 2504) and the subsequent `tree_divergence_for_species(labels, trees)` call (line 2507) run unguarded. Inside it, `_patristic_distance_matrix` builds `clades = {clade.name: clade for clade in tree.get_terminals()}` (line 2366) then does `clades[labels[i]]` (line 2371) with no membership check. IQ-TREE's well-documented default behavior removes duplicate/identical sequences from the tree search (only kept with `-keep-ident`, which is not passed in `run_iqtree`'s subprocess args at lines 2353-2354), so a species with any duplicate CDS across S/M/L can produce a treefile missing a label from `labels`, raising an uncaught KeyError. `run_phylogenetics_stage` (def at 2555) calls `_analyze_species` in a plain loop at line 2595-2596 with no try/except, and `run_pipeline`'s call at line 3294 (`phylo_rows = run_phylogenetics_stage(...)`) is likewise unwrapped, and there is no try/except anywhere in `run_pipeline` or `main` (confirmed by reading lines 3368-3381), so the KeyError propagates and aborts the whole run before the 'Writing outputs' block at line 3301, which writes ortho_accession_table and the other core tables.

### [2] all_hanta.py:2496 (CONFIRMED)
_analyze_species only wraps the MAFFT/IQ-TREE subprocess calls in try/except; the downstream Phylo.read, tree_divergence_for_species, dendropy RF computation, and classify_reassortment_call/bootstrap_support_for_pair calls (lines 2504-2536) run outside any exception handler, and run_pipeline has no try/except around run_phylogenetics_stage either.
Failure scenario: If any post-alignment step raises for a given species -- e.g. bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` (line ~2416) hitting StopIteration on a tip-label/tree mismatch, Phylo.read failing on an unexpected treefile format, or dendropy's shared TaxonNamespace/encode_bipartitions choking on a degenerate tree -- the exception propagates uncaught through _analyze_species -> run_phylogenetics_stage -> run_pipeline -> main(), which has no top-level try/except. Because run_pipeline (as of this diff) runs the entire `if args.phylogenetics:` block *before* 'Writing outputs' (line ~3290), the crash aborts the whole pipeline and no parquet tables at all are written for that invocation -- not just the reassortment table but ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_ml_feature_matrix, etc. -- directly contradicting the stated invariant ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run, it just marks that species' isolates failed and moves on') and README's 'Nothing is silently dropped' / 'a species/segment failure never aborts the run' claims for a run enabling --phylogenetics on real-world data with any edge-case tree.
Verifier evidence: Same structural gap as [0], described more broadly: lines 2504-2551 (Phylo.read, tree_divergence_for_species, the dendropy RF block at 2512-2525, and the per-member classify_reassortment_call/bootstrap_support_for_pair loop at 2527-2551) all sit after the try/except that ends at line 2503, so any exception there (e.g. bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` at line 2417 raising StopIteration, or a dendropy TaxonNamespace/encode_bipartitions failure at lines 2512-2519) is uncaught. run_phylogenetics_stage's per-species loop (2593-2596) and its call site in run_pipeline (line 3294) have no surrounding try/except, and main()/run_pipeline have none either (verified lines 3368-3381 and the run_pipeline body around 3290-3309), so the crash happens before 'Writing outputs' (line 3301) and no parquet tables at all are written for that invocation, contradicting the stated per-unit isolation invariant.

### [3] all_hanta.py:2504 (CONFIRMED, cleanup)
The per-species try/except in _analyze_species only wraps run_mafft/run_iqtree, not the Phylo.read/tree-distance/dendropy-RF/bootstrap-lookup code that follows, and run_pipeline sequences the whole --phylogenetics stage before the 'Writing outputs' block with no enclosing try/except anywhere up to main().
Failure scenario: If IQ-TREE succeeds but the .treefile can't be parsed by Bio.Phylo (unexpected characters, IQ-TREE writing an unrooted trifurcation Newick variant it doesn't like, truncated write on a full disk), or dendropy.Tree.get()/treecompare.symmetric_difference chokes because the three trees' tip sets don't line up exactly, or bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=...))` raises StopIteration for a missing tip -- none of that is caught. The exception propagates out of _analyze_species, out of run_phylogenetics_stage, and out of run_pipeline uncaught, crashing the whole program with a traceback. Because this block (all_hanta.py lines ~3290-3298) runs before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all the safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, ortho_isolate_table, ortho_risk_table, the ML tables, etc., a single species hitting this gap means a --phylogenetics run produces ZERO output files at all -- not just a missing/failed reassortment row for that species -- directly contradicting the code's own docstring ('a species/segment failure never aborts the run... the same per-unit error isolation transform_one_record uses') and the README's 'nothing is silently dropped' / byte-for-byte-unaffected-default claims, since the only way to get any output on a --phylogenetics run is for every single one of potentially dozens of species-level tree builds to hit no post-tree-build exception at all.
Verifier evidence: In _analyze_species (all_hanta.py ~2496-2503), only run_mafft/run_iqtree are wrapped: `try: run_mafft(...); treefile = run_iqtree(...) except Exception as exc: ... return [_phylo_row(...,'failed',...) for c in members]`. Immediately after that except block, unwrapped code follows: `trees[segment] = Phylo.read(str(treefile), 'newick')` (line 2504), the dendropy TaxonNamespace/Tree.get()/encode_bipartitions()/treecompare.symmetric_difference() block (lines 2512-2525), and classify_reassortment_call -> bootstrap_support_for_pair's `next(tree.find_clades(name=label_a))` (line 2417, which raises StopIteration if no match) -- none of these are inside a try/except. run_phylogenetics_stage calls `_analyze_species(...)` in a plain for-loop with no try/except (`rows.extend(_analyze_species(species, members, ...))`, lines 2593-2596). In run_pipeline, the phylogenetics block (`if args.phylogenetics: ... phylo_rows = run_phylogenetics_stage(...); safe_write_parquet(...)`) runs with no enclosing try/except and is placed before `logging.info("Writing outputs")` and all subsequent safe_write_parquet calls for ortho_accession_table, ortho_species_table, etc. main() also has no try/except around run_pipeline. So any exception raised in the unwrapped post-tree-build code for any one species propagates uncaught all the way out of main(), crashing the process before any output table is written -- exactly as described.

### [4] all_hanta.py:2569 (CONFIRMED, cleanup)
_phylo_row hardcodes n_taxa_in_tree=0 for 'species_below_min_taxa' rows instead of the species' actual candidate count.
Failure scenario: A user filtering ortho_reassortment_table.parquet on n_taxa_in_species_tree to see how close an excluded species was to the --phylo-min-taxa threshold (e.g. to decide whether to lower it and re-run) sees 0 for every below-threshold species regardless of whether it had 1 candidate or phylo_min_taxa-1 candidates, silently discarding information that group_candidates_by_species already computed (it logs 'only {len(members)} candidate(s), need {min_taxa}' but that count never reaches the per-isolate output row).
Verifier evidence: In run_phylogenetics_stage, rows for species that fall below --phylo-min-taxa are built with: `_phylo_row(c, c.isolate.species_name, 0, "species_below_min_taxa", "") for c in candidates if c.isolate.isolate_key not in grouped_keys` (all_hanta.py:2588) -- the third positional arg to _phylo_row (n_taxa_in_tree, mapped to the output column `n_taxa_in_species_tree` at line 2448) is a hardcoded literal 0 regardless of how many candidates that species actually had. group_candidates_by_species (lines 2281-2302) does compute len(members) per species and even logs it via species_drop_reasons (e.g. 'only {len(members)} candidate(s), need {min_taxa}' at line 2299), but that count is never threaded back to the per-isolate row -- only the formatted log string is returned in the Counter, not a species->count mapping usable by _phylo_row. So every isolate belonging to an under-threshold species gets n_taxa_in_species_tree=0 in ortho_reassortment_table.parquet, whether the species actually had 0, 1, or phylo_min_taxa-1 candidates, exactly as the finding describes.

## Instructions
Return decisions about findings BY INDEX — never re-emit finding text.
1. For each distinct defect, emit one decision with its index. When several findings describe the same defect (same root cause), keep one entry and list the others in its merge array.
2. Order decisions most-severe first. Correctness bugs always outrank cleanup findings.
3. Keep at most 10 decisions; omit the least severe beyond the cap.
4. Write a 2-3 sentence summary of the review.

Structured output only.

Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact can declare — calling the user's claude.ai connectors (MCP) from the page, and future abilities. Load this BEFORE passing `capabilities` to the Artifact tool or writing any `window.claude.mcp` code.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes; bootstraps this repo's project verify skill if none exists yet. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
